title: Why Hellboy Breaks His Own Horns
description: Hellboy was meant to bring the apocalypse. He chose another job. A short comic-lore explanation of his stone right hand and the horn-breaking scene in Wake the Devil. This follows Mike Mignola’s original comics, not a movie adaptation.
hook: Hellboy was born to end the world. His response was to break off his own horns.
payoff: He breaks them off. He's been told what he was born to do. He chooses who he wants to be.

units.speaker: Host
units.text: Hellboy was born to end the world. His response was to break off his own horns.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: An occult ritual brought him to Earth as a child. Professor Broom took him in and raised him.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: He grew up protecting people from monsters. Then he learned what that huge right hand was made for.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: That stone hand is the key to freeing the Ogdru Jahad, ancient monsters that could destroy the world.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: In Wake the Devil, Hecate calls him the Beast of the Apocalypse. His horns grow back.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: Accepting that destiny would mean turning on the people who raised him. The monster hunter would become their destroyer.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: He breaks them off. He's been told what he was born to do. He chooses who he wants to be.

units.speaker: Host
units.text: Hell wanted a king. It got a monster hunter.
